title: Wide cross-platform discovery pass 42
summary: Personally review 40 cross-platform roots: add 37 source-backed projects and record three non-promotions.
notes: Root personally ran 54 searches returning 455 hits and 451 distinct repository URLs, and inspected 40 selected roots. Add 37 projects with three explicit non-promotions. Coverage spans classic computers, consoles, games, source archives, disassembly/decompilation, source translators, assemblers, debuggers, hardware diagnostics, format/media/asset tools and educational development code. No discovery worker was used; no upstream code or media was executed. Broad coverage is not exhaustion of every platform. Current catalogue snapshot pinned to 35cb7328d65b1a2bd422e36e0fc8c0107f2049c4, with older cached activity history only for local staging; trusted-main validation remains required. Ingestion findings: broad unquoted platform searches return unrelated token matches, so six quoted-platform repair queries followed. Equal repository basenames can be unrelated (two beebasm roots); a cross assembler ROM runs on 65C02 despite 68000 in its name; CP/M-like 6502 OS is not 8080-compatible. decomp names and zero placeholders do not prove recovered C or semantic completion; matching module counts are distinct from playable full-ROM output. Preserve conversion direction, format/per-game limits, TODOs and proprietary-input requirements. Sparse/empty/inherited READMEs need implementation inspection. Recursive tree retrieval failed for khdays twice; a commit lookup and targeted file reads recovered evidence without treating a transport failure as no source. Pinned commit IDs were checked against retrieved trees before evidence links were emitted. Snowboard Kids 2 has an unfetchable shiftability link, so its guarantee is not repeated as verified. API success with an empty README can be a genuinely empty file, distinct from oversized Contents truncation. Schema validation, not submission packaging alone, is required before publication.

sources.reason: Related native ROM sources include serial/user-port filing systems and restored sideways-RAM management. Board-specific features are conditionally omitted; HostFS serial polling has timing limitations.

Source examples and reusable graphics routines with Node/VSCode tasks that assemble, replace files in a disk image and launch AppleWin. This is a development workflow, not a new assembler or game reconstruction.

CMD/BASIC/raw disassembly, annotation/JSON IR, assembler and deterministic emulator feed observed coverage back into analysis. Recursive descent leaves unreached bytes unknown and diagnoses overlaps. Web and MCP interfaces share core libraries.
Converts among D64, G64, P64, FDI, NIB and KryoFlux streams, with track/pulse diagnostics. Sector representations cannot preserve physical information absent from their format.
Core track/sector writer with CBM DOS directory, extra-track and separator modules; supports per-file placement/interleave. Unknown options can be silently ignored because modules interpret them.

macOS converter implements platform-specific image layouts and native exports rather than merely retro visual filters. Inspected CPC source exposes mode-specific packing and palette processing; other mode and disk claims are upstream documentation, not exhaustive validation.
Annotated reconstruction of the BBC sideways ROM for a 68000 cross assembler. Python explicitly loads the ROM as 65C02: 68000 is the generated instruction set, not the CPU executing this ROM.
Port of UNLZEXE supporting LZEXE 0.90/0.91 MZ/ZM images, reconstructed relocation tables and bounds-checked input. Not a universal DOS unpacker or C decompiler.
Extracts/edits Shift-JIS text and patches halfwidth display for vanilla VG2 and the Perfect Collection revision. Offsets differ between versions and must be re-extracted.

Sparse source-only translation workspace. Inspected Lodoss 1 reinserter enforces field byte lengths, pads text, applies fixed-offset edits and writes new game/scenario HDM images. Description mentions both games, but inspected implementation does not establish complete support for Lodoss 2.
Native IOCS-based CRT/LCD test patterns enumerate 15/24/31 kHz modes and color/VRAM layouts. It is a display diagnostic, not a source reconstruction or universal monitor compatibility test.

Generated annotated listing with address-bound notes, explicit indirect entry hints, graphics decoders and openMSX VRAM comparisons. Full 32 KiB explanation/matching and 21 tests are upstream measurements, not independent verification.

Historical Euphoric-associated format tools include BASIC tokenization, assemblers, plotter rendering and disk conversion. This root adds smaller Sedoric-image configuration support. Empty primary README does not mean absent implementation.
Loads tape blocks on the original machine and writes numbered disk files; includes multipart and slow-tape modes. This is distinct from modern WAV decoding.
Disk-based macro assembler supports Z80/Z180/Z280 instruction sets, conditional assembly and REL output suitable for L80/LINK. Source includes explicit relocatable-record generation.
Author-maintained CP/M-like BIOS/BDOS/CCP and native utilities including assembler, BASIC and Forth. Nearly compatible disk directory is not 8080 binary compatibility; programs load at $0200.

Mechanical assembly translator maps instructions and selected BDOS/reboot calls. No macros, incomplete ! line separation and 255-character line limit; manual repair can be necessary. It is not CPU emulation.
Banked disassembly of the unlicensed 9 Fighter NES title, not Capcom arcade Street Fighter III. Build scripts assemble named banks and append graphics/header data.

Collection of game-specific graphics/text/tile decompressors and some compressors. Inspected Ardy Lightfoot source uses a fixed ROM name, fixed offset and small buffers; not an automatic generic SNES format detector.
Native external-clock link receiver prints ASCII/hex bytes via serial and VBlank interrupts. Source warns of a high-volume data bug in its 255-byte queue; not a lossless general serial analyser.
Modified Macro-Assembler AS used by Mega Drive Sonic disassemblies. Includes genuine code generators, not game source itself; historical host portability statements are not current verified builds.

US MK-81019 analysis publishes function maps, provisional names, Ghidra scripts and cross-overlay transfer tools, but no recovered C or game binaries. Zero placeholders is not semantic completeness; thousands of names remain provisional.
Early archive/model inspection and editing for Okami data_pc, including scene viewer and standalone utilities. PlayStation search provenance must not become a claim of PS2 media compatibility.

Matching reconstruction and asset extraction from an owned big-endian ROM, explicitly not a PC port. Code still contains unknown names and partial structure views; a matching build is not semantic completion.
Work-in-progress game reconstruction with named combat routines and data annotations. Human-editable asset conversion and further recovery remain unfinished.

Packs/extracts .neo and MAME/Darksoft layouts, edits header metadata, handles C interleaving and optional P-bank half swap. Auto-detection is a reset-vector plausibility heuristic, not proof for every hack or unusual image.
Converts palette, CHR and raw nametable data into PC Engine assembly, with an example display program. RLE nametables are unsupported and palette mapping is manually adjustable.

Reconstructs missing pieces around original FFLSRC.ZIP and modernizes build tooling. Retail versus modified/no-trailer outputs are separate; retail identity includes trailer bytes and regenerated security prefix.

Image conversion covers CEL/IMAG/LRFORM, palettes and selected NFS containers. No dithering, incomplete CEL option combinations and directional format limits remain. ANIM output and NFS wwww writing are TODOs despite broad introductory wording.

EU YKGP ARM9/overlay reconstruction reports all 306 modules matching, while distinguishing C, library assembly and two CLZ exceptions. Matching modules are not a playable rebuilt ROM; naming/structure consolidation remains ongoing and reported counters have different denominators.

Extracts ARM7/ARM9/overlay memory sections and generates XML analysis projects with optional symbols/I/O labels. Optional BSS filling creates modeled placeholder bytes, not recovered original initialized data.

Narrow scripts extract the Snail Maze path from a particular 8 KiB v1.3 BIOS and inject an export-cartridge header. Hardcoded layout/checksum assumptions are not a general arbitrary-ROM repair service.
Historical Gemini 2 source snapshot recovered from an old Atari TT, including native TOS/GEM support code. Preservation of a snapshot does not establish a clean modern build or completeness.

Browser parser handles PICT resource/file framing, PackBits and selected drawing records. Inspected implementation contains unfinished/debugging notes; do not infer complete QuickDraw opcode fidelity from picture extraction.
Provides resource-fork and Finder-info access across native named forks, extended attributes and Windows AFP streams. Despite the name, it is not an Apple Filing Protocol network server.
Portable 6502-family assembler with BBC BASIC-like directives, loops and expressions; writes assembled files directly into DFS SSD/DSD images and can create boot entries.

Reusable Mode 7 routines and small standalone examples, plus translated examples from Discovering BBC Micro Machine Code. This is an educational code library, not a fork or alternative implementation of the BeebAsm assembler.

Inspected root is chiefly Workbench icon/theme assets and bundled utilities, with small icon-generation command workflows. No distinct reversing/restoration implementation established; do not misclassify packaged binaries as available utility source.
An early read/echo loop and string helpers are present, but lexer and parser return immediately. Retain the project lead without advertising a functioning Lisp interpreter.

Detailed format notes with unknown fields, but no parser implementation, named game/version verification or validation corpus established. Retain as a format-research source rather than a working general PSP model toolkit.
